risk: Decisions could not be checked or challenged: nothing recorded what the system decided, when, or why
who_is_harmed: Residents whose reports are mis-sorted; managers who must explain decisions
evidence: Before Week 6 no decision was logged anywhere
mitigation: Decision log: every classification and forecast run is written to governance/logs/decisions.csv with reason and rules version

risk: Personal details (phone, ID numbers, emails, names, house numbers) could be copied into the decision log
who_is_harmed: Residents who include personal details in reports
evidence: Residents write free text; the log stores a summary of it
mitigation: Summaries go through Role 3's mask_personal_info() and are cut to 80 characters before writing; pattern-based masking can still miss unusual formats (see R3-02)

risk: Managers may treat forecasts and urgency scores as exact facts
who_is_harmed: Residents in areas or reports that the numbers get wrong
evidence: Forecast is off by about 4 reports a week; classifier got 4 of 30 tricky reports wrong
mitigation: Transparency notes and model cards state accuracy and limits; dashboard shows likely ranges

risk: The decision log has no retention limit, so it keeps growing and holds data longer than needed
who_is_harmed: Residents
evidence: Each full run adds about 4,000 rows; POPIA expects data to be kept no longer than needed
mitigation: Rows older than 365 days are deleted automatically whenever the log is written (REPORT_RADAR_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS to change it); tested

risk: Hotspot rankings were not recorded in the decision log
who_is_harmed: Residents of areas ranked as quiet
evidence: Only the ranked table was saved, overwritten on every run
mitigation: Every hotspot run now logs the ranking, number of areas and why that number was chosen; tested

risk: Reports written in unsupported languages or wording can be assigned a low default urgency
who_is_harmed: Residents using languages and dialects not represented in keyword rules
evidence: Before changes, synthetic language group category accuracy was 25% and urgency accuracy was 25% across 60 reports
mitigation: Review non-English reports with a fluent speaker; expand phrases using reviewed samples; route uncertain cases for human review

risk: Urgency can be under-scored when elderly, disabled, or pregnant residents are not recognized
who_is_harmed: Elderly, disabled, pregnant residents and caregivers
evidence: Before changes, exact urgency accuracy was 20% (2 of 10) on synthetic vulnerable-group reports
mitigation: Use reviewed vulnerability terms; audit urgency for these groups and retain human escalation for safety-critical reports

risk: Curated translation examples may create false confidence if translations are wrong or coverage is narrow
who_is_harmed: Residents whose phrasing differs from tested samples
evidence: All non-English test IDs are CHECK-marked; translations have not yet been speaker-verified; after metrics use the same 70 curated rows
mitigation: Ask fluent speakers to verify examples using translation_review.csv and apply_translation_review.py; track per-language outcomes and retest variants before relying on scores

risk: Raw report-count hotspot rankings can direct more crews to already busy wards and leave quieter wards waiting longer
who_is_harmed: Residents in wards with fewer reports or barriers to reporting
evidence: Synthetic sample: Old Alexandra has 1,188 reports and Tsutsumani 233; their resolved urgent medians are 23.55 and 44.30 hours
mitigation: Include urgency and reports per verified household count in prioritization; retain a minimum service floor for every ward; review ward-level outcomes

risk: Urgent reports may have persistently longer resolution times in some wards
who_is_harmed: Residents needing urgent services in Tsutsumani, Setswetla, and Far East Bank
evidence: Synthetic sample: urgent medians are 44.30, 37.45, and 36.85 hours respectively, above the 35.33-hour screening threshold
mitigation: Review urgent backlogs and crew allocation by ward; set and monitor a response standard; investigate operational causes before drawing conclusions

risk: Illustrative household assumptions may create misleading reports-per-1,000 rates
who_is_harmed: Residents and managers comparing wards using unsupported denominators
evidence: No census or official household counts were supplied; current ward values are explicit placeholders
mitigation: Replace placeholders with current municipality-approved household estimates matched to ward boundaries; record source and date and recalculate

risk: Personal details written in report text could be stored, shown or sent to an outside LLM
who_is_harmed: Residents who include phone numbers, ID numbers, emails or names in reports
evidence: Scan of 3,994 synthetic reports found 0 matches, but real residents write free text; the optional LLM classifier sends residents' words to an outside company
mitigation: mask_personal_info() in governance/privacy.py masks phones, ID numbers, emails, house numbers and names before reports are logged or sent to an LLM; covered by tests

risk: Masking is pattern-based and can miss personal details in unusual formats, names without a title, or other languages
who_is_harmed: Residents whose details are not recognised and masked
evidence: Tests only cover made-up examples in the formats we listed; no names are recognised unless they follow a title or 'my name is'
mitigation: Do not send unmasked text to an LLM; extend patterns using reviewed samples in each language; keep human review of flagged reports

risk: Health and vulnerability details and exact coordinates could identify a household or expose special personal information
who_is_harmed: Elderly and disabled residents, patients, and households at exact report locations
evidence: Descriptions mention clinics, elderly and disabled residents; every report stores exact latitude and longitude
mitigation: Limit who can see raw reports; show ward-level or rounded locations on shared views; apply stronger protection to special personal information in real data

risk: No retention limit, access control, or way for residents to see and correct their reports
who_is_harmed: Residents
evidence: Data card records no retention period and no dashboard access control; nothing lets a resident request or correct their report
mitigation: Agree a retention period with Role 4 (e.g. 12 months, see R4-04); add access control before real data is used; set up a process for access and correction requests

risk: The live public dashboard shows residents' report text word for word, so personal details in a report would be visible to anyone with the link
who_is_harmed: Residents who include names, phone numbers or addresses in reports
evidence: The Reports tab shows each description unmasked; the app is public at reportradar.streamlit.app; safe today only because the data is synthetic
mitigation: Before any real data: mask descriptions with mask_personal_info() on the dashboard and put the app behind a login

risk: Managers may act on the headline summary (e.g. 'no surge expected') without reading the likely range or the limits
who_is_harmed: Residents whose problems fall outside the forecast or the busiest areas
evidence: The summary box gives single numbers first; caveats sit in expanders and the Risk & compliance tab
mitigation: Likely ranges next to every number, 'How this was decided' notes and model cards; review the summary wording with a manager

risk: The risk register is scored by the same team that built the system, so risks may be under-rated
who_is_harmed: Residents affected by risks the team did not see or scored too low
evidence: All 19 risks were found and scored by the five team members; no outside review yet
mitigation: Ask the facilitator or another team to review the register and the Week 6 risk report

risk: All findings come from synthetic data, so the fairness, bias and accuracy results may not hold for real reports in Alexandra
who_is_harmed: Residents if real decisions are based on these results
evidence: data/reports.csv is generated; the busy wards, surges and wording were built into it
mitigation: Label every result as synthetic; test on a consented sample of real reports before use

risk: A supervisor may approve an unsafe or misrouted report without reading it
who_is_harmed: Residents waiting for a serious or misrouted problem to be handled
evidence: A supervisor can approve a ticket from a short decision control; this workflow has not yet been tested with real supervisors
mitigation: Show the masked description and urgency before each decision; require reasons for rejection and reassignment; review saved decisions at the halfway check-in

risk: Residents without internet access or a suitable device may be unable to use the online form
who_is_harmed: Residents without reliable internet, data, or a suitable device
evidence: The Week 7 form is an online channel and no offline reporting route has been tested
mitigation: Keep phone and in-person reporting available; do not make the online form the only route; include an access question in the outside-team usability check

risk: Automation can hide a step that quietly gives wrong results (for example a wrong team or urgency) because nothing visibly fails
who_is_harmed: Residents whose reports are sent to the wrong queue or given too long a deadline
evidence: process_report() runs every step without a person; the classifier gets 4 of 30 tricky reports wrong
mitigation: Every step is written to the decision log with its reason; supervisors approve urgent and unclear reports; review the log and the Intake desk queue weekly

risk: Temporary stand-ins for routing, approvals and emails could stay in use after the real modules should have replaced them
who_is_harmed: Residents and teams, if simplified rules decide real tickets
evidence: workflow/fallbacks.py is used whenever a teammate's function is missing
mitigation: The decision log names every stand-in used; delete each stand-in as soon as the real module lands

risk: A crash part-way through could leave a report half-processed or lost
who_is_harmed: Residents whose reports disappear
evidence: A report passes through 7 steps, any of which can fail
mitigation: A failed step still saves the ticket to the supervisor's approval queue with a note and emails the supervisor; the tickets file is written then swapped so a crash can't leave half a file; tested

risk: Supervisor approval queue may become a bottleneck and delay urgent work
who_is_harmed: Residents with urgent reports waiting for supervisor review
evidence: Urgent and unclear tickets wait for supervisor decisions; approval queue capacity and wait time have not yet been measured
mitigation: Track approval queue size and age; set a review-time target; arrange backup approvers and escalate tickets that exceed the target

risk: Supervisors may reject reports from some wards more often than others
who_is_harmed: Residents whose reports come from wards with higher rejection rates
evidence: Approval and rejection outcomes have not yet been audited by ward
mitigation: Review approval, rejection, and reassignment rates by ward at regular intervals; investigate differences with supervisors and provide a clear review route for rejected tickets

risk: An email goes to the wrong team or supervisor, so the right people are not told or the wrong people see a report
who_is_harmed: Residents whose urgent reports are not seen in time
evidence: Each email goes to the team the router chose, so a routing mistake sends the email there too; all addresses are still placeholders
mitigation: Emails use masked text only; supervisor gets every approval and overdue email; real team addresses must be checked with the municipality before sending is switched on

risk: A resident is emailed who did not want contact, or has no way to stop updates
who_is_harmed: Residents who give an email address
evidence: The email box is optional and only used for updates, but there is no unsubscribe step; if sending is switched on the address passes through a mail provider
mitigation: Email is optional and explained on the form; address is never saved; only one email (received) goes to residents; add a stop-updates process before real use

risk: Real emails are sent by accident, or an email password is saved in the repository
who_is_harmed: Residents and the municipality
evidence: Sending needs all three SMTP settings; a test confirms nothing is sent without them; outbox files are ignored by git
mitigation: Default is save-only; no passwords in code; outbox and tickets file are in .gitignore; review every push for secrets

risk: A failed email goes unnoticed, so a resident or team is never told
who_is_harmed: Residents and teams waiting for updates
evidence: If sending fails the email is still saved and the log says 'outbox (smtp failed)', but nobody is alerted
mitigation: Failures never lose the ticket; add a dashboard warning or daily check of failed emails; supervisor overdue emails act as a backstop

risk: A report routed to the wrong service team may wait longer before the correct crew receives it
who_is_harmed: Residents waiting for repairs; crews receiving misrouted work
evidence: Routing is based on a fixed category-to-team table; unclear reports go to the Intake desk
mitigation: Review misrouted tickets and reassignments weekly; update routing_rules.csv when service ownership changes
